column2: A slot machine: reels of blurred ROM symbols (katakana, arrows, the yen sign) spin behind a window, the lever is pulled at :00, and the reels stop one by one on the new time with a bounce. The slow glass's smear is the reel blur. On the hour a jackpot: lights chase and coins pour.

Sokoban: a tiny warehouse worker pushes the cell-aligned blocks of a block-digit face around the glass. Each minute it pushes the parts of the old digit into the shape of the new one, with the satisfying clunk of each push. The cell seams are the floor tiles.
The Nokia Snake game: the snake's own body coils into the time. Each minute an apple appears, the snake uncoils to chase it, eats it, and re-coils into the new digits.

Whack-a-mole: moles pop up out of holes holding up the digits. At :00 a mallet whacks the mole with the old digit, which ducks down dazed with stars, and a new mole pops up with the new one. Moles fidget, peek and taunt between turns.

A hamster runs in a wheel that powers the clock: its running is the seconds and it pedals the digits round like a counter. At :00 it puts on a sprint; on the hour it falls off exhausted, eats a seed and climbs back in.

Dominoes: the digits are built from standing domino tiles. At :00 a finger flicks the first and the chain topples across the glass in a wave, and the fallen tiles show the new time in their pips, then are stood back up.

Matchstick puzzles: the digits are made of matches. Each minute a hand moves the fewest matches needed to turn the old time into the new one, like the classic "move one match" puzzle. A match may be struck and burn for the hour show.

A snail crawls the full length of the glass in exactly one hour, and its silvery slime trail is the minutes. It has a personality: it stops to eat a leaf, retreats into its shell when startled, and on the hour it reaches the end and a new snail sets off.

A dot-matrix printer: the print head sweeps along the row, hammering the time into the paper dot by dot with the head's buzzy rhythm. The paper feeds up through the two rows each minute and the old time scrolls off the top.

A little train runs through both rows: the carriages carry the digits as cargo. Each minute it pulls into a station, a crane swaps the cargo for the new digit, the whistle blows and it pulls out. The scenery (ROM stations, signals, trees) streams past.

Chinese lion dance (舞狮): a lion head with blinking eyes and a fluttering beard chases a ball that carries the digit, bobbing to the drum beat each second. On the minute it catches and "eats" the old digit and spits out the new one; on the hour firecrackers go off.

Tug of war: the two rows are two rival teams (two rows that disagree), the rope's knot sways with each heave as the seconds. At :00 one team wins, the losers tumble, and the new minute is pulled across.
